title: The Parisian house that defined the 'New Look'
clues: This French luxury brand was founded in 1946, just after WWII ended.
Their debut collection was nicknamed the 'New Look' and featured cinched waists and full skirts.
The brand sells haute couture but is also known for J'adore perfume and Sauvage cologne.
Its logo is the founder's last name in capital letters, with four letters.
It is part of LVMH and its flagship store sits at 30 Avenue Montaigne, Paris.

title: The fruit that changed personal tech forever
clues: This American company was founded in 1976 in a California garage.
Its first mass-market computer featured a rainbow logo.
It launched a music player in 2001 that said '1000 songs in your pocket'.
The company designs the iPhone, iPad, and Mac, and runs the App Store.
Its current HQ is a ring-shaped campus called Apple Park in Cupertino.

title: The swoosh that runs the world
clues: This company started in 1964 as Blue Ribbon Sports distributing Japanese shoes.
Its logo was designed by a student for just $35 and represents the wing of a Greek goddess.
The 'Just Do It' slogan debuted in 1988.
Air Jordan sneakers and Dri-FIT apparel are two of its biggest product lines.
It is headquartered near Beaverton, Oregon and sponsors athletes worldwide.

title: The red can that taught the world to sing
clues: This drink was invented in 1886 by a pharmacist in Atlanta, Georgia.
Its secret formula is famously stored in a vault at the World of Coca-Cola museum.
The brand helped popularize the modern image of Santa Claus in red and white.
It owns Sprite, Fanta, and Minute Maid in addition to its namesake soda.
The script logo has remained nearly unchanged for over 130 years.

title: The electric car company named after an inventor
clues: This company was founded in 2003 and named after a Serbian-American electrical engineer.
Its first production car was a Roadster based on a Lotus chassis.
The Model S, 3, X, and Y spell out a word when listed together.
It operates a network of Supercharger stations for its vehicles.
The CEO is also known for SpaceX and buying a Marketing platform in 2022.

title: Golden arches that circle the globe
clues: This restaurant chain began in 1940 as a BBQ drive-in run by two brothers in California.
A milkshake machine salesman named Ray Kroc turned it into a global franchise.
The Big Mac was introduced in 1967 and has its own economic index.
Its clown mascot was retired in the 2010s but was iconic for decades.
It serves over 69 million customers daily in more than 100 countries.

title: From bookstore to everything store
clues: This company started in 1994 selling books out of a garage in Bellevue, Washington.
Its logo features an arrow pointing from A to Z, symbolizing all products.
Prime membership launched in 2005 offering two-day shipping.
AWS, its cloud computing division, powers a huge portion of the internet.
The founder went to space on a rocket built by his other company in 2021.

title: The mouse that built an empire
clues: This company was founded in 1923 by two brothers as a cartoon studio.
Steamboat Willie in 1928 introduced its most famous mascot to the world.
It opened its first theme park in Anaheim, California in 1955.
It now owns Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm, and 20th Century Studios.
The corporate logo is a stylized castle, often Cinderella Castle.

title: The app that put filters on the world
clues: This app launched in October 2010 as a photo-sharing platform.
It was originally exclusive to iPhone and reached 1 million users in 2 months.
Facebook acquired it for $1 billion in 2012 before it had any revenue.
Stories, Reels, and the heart-shaped Like button are core features.
Its logo evolved from a vintage camera to a gradient square.

title: The siren that sells a third place
clues: This chain was founded in 1971 in Seattle's Pike Place Market.
It is named after a character in the novel Moby-Dick.
The green logo features a twin-tailed mermaid called a siren.
It popularized terms like Venti, Grande, and Frappuccino globally.
Customers can order using a mobile app and collect Stars for rewards.

title: The prancing horse from Maranello
clues: This Italian automaker was founded in 1939 by a former race car driver.
Its logo is a black prancing horse on a yellow background.
The brand's Formula 1 team is the oldest and most successful in F1 history.
LaFerrari and the 488 are two of its modern supercar models.
All its road cars are painted red by default, a color called Rosso Corsa.

title: The three stripes from Bavaria
clues: This German company was founded in 1949 after a split between two brothers.
Its name comes from the founder's nickname, Adi, plus the first three letters of his last name.
The trefoil logo and three-stripe design are recognized worldwide.
It signed Run-DMC in the 1980s, one of the first major hip-hop endorsement deals.
The rival company founded by the other brother is also a major Marketing brand.

title: The company that killed the video store
clues: This company started in 1997 by mailing DVDs in red envelopes.
Its Marketing service launched in 2007 and changed how people watch TV.
House of Cards in 2013 was its first original series.
The 'Are you still watching' prompt is both loved and memed by users.
Its sound logo, called the 'ta-dum', plays before every show.

title: The verb that became a noun
clues: This company began as a research project at Stanford in 1996 called BackRub.
Its name is a play on the mathematical term 'googol' meaning 10 to the 100th power.
The homepage is famous for its minimalist design and colorful logo.
Gmail, Maps, and Chrome are all products from this company.
Its parent company, formed in 2015, is called Alphabet.

title: The double-G from Florence
clues: This Italian fashion house was founded in 1921 by a former hotel porter.
The interlocking double-G logo represents the founder's initials.
Its bamboo-handle bag was created in 1947 due to material shortages.
Alessandro Michele's tenure brought maximalist designs and huge growth after 2015.
It is now part of the Kering group alongside Yves Saint Laurent and Balenciaga.

title: The drink that gives you wings
clues: This energy drink was inspired by a Thai drink called Krating Daeng.
An Austrian entrepreneur co-founded the company in 1987 and adapted it for the West.
Its slogan promises to 'give you wings' and is known globally.
The brand owns multiple sports teams, including an F1 team and soccer clubs.
It sponsors extreme events like cliff diving and the Stratos space jump.

title: The card company that captured consoles
clues: This Japanese company was founded in 1889 to produce handmade playing cards.
It entered video games in the 1970s and released Donkey Kong in 1981.
The NES launched in 1985 and revived the home console market.
Mario, Zelda, and Pokémon are franchises owned by this company.
The Switch console released in 2017 is both handheld and docked.

title: The flat-pack maze with meatballs
clues: This company was founded in 1943 in Sweden by a 17-year-old.
Its name is an acronym from the founder's initials and his farm and village.
Stores are famous for their one-way showroom layout and warehouse pickup.
It sells Marketing that customers assemble themselves from flat boxes.
The restaurant inside serves Swedish meatballs and lingonberry jam.

title: The card that goes everywhere you want to be
clues: This financial services company started as BankAmericard in 1958.
It was renamed in 1976 to a word that suggests universal acceptance.
The logo is blue and gold, and used to feature those colors in a striped banner.
It is not a bank but a network that processes transactions between banks.
It sponsors the Olympics and FIFA World Cup as the exclusive Marketing partner.

title: Because the world is worth it
clues: This French company was founded in 1909 by a chemist who created hair dye.
Its name comes from the French word for 'gold' and the founder's first product.
The slogan 'Because I'm worth it' launched in 1971 and became iconic.
It owns Maybelline, Lancôme, Garnier, and Kiehl's among many others.
It is the world's largest Marketing company by revenue.
